 This Appeal Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The claimant is in appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT at Bidar (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.364/2014, vide judgment and award dated 22.03.2018 2.

The impugned judgment and award discloses that the claimant suffered injuries in a road accident, when he was travelling in a light goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-25//TRE-9431 which was dashed against by a tractor bearing registration No.AP-25/T-4401 (henceforth referred as 'offending vehicle').
The claimant claimed that he suffered injuries on his right leg and on other parts of the body and was shifted to Government Hospital, Bidar, where he was treated from 23.02.2013 to 06.03.2013.
He claimed that he was a qualified driver and was earning Rs.3,000/- per month and daily allowance of Rs.250/- which he used to maintain himself and his family members.
He therefore filed a claim petition under NC: 2023:KHC-K:1450 Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
3. The insurer contested the claim petition and claimed that the offending vehicle was implicated in the case on the basis of false complaint registered against the driver of the offending vehicle.
It also claimed that the driver of the light goods vehicle was negligent and was responsible for the accident.
It also claimed that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid licence.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P20.
The claimant examined a doctor as PW.2, who deposed that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 20% to the whole body.

The Tribunal assessed the disability suffered by the claimant at 10% and considered notional NC:
2023:KHC-K:1450 income at a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month and awarded the following compensation:
Towards pain and suffering Rs.30,000/- Towards loss of future Rs.1,53,600/-
income Towards loss of income Rs.24,000/-
during laid up period Towards loss of amenities Rs.10,000/- Towards medical expenses Rs.1,500/-
Towards attendant, Rs.3,000/-
conveyance, food extra nourishment charges Total Rs.2,22,100/-

5. The Tribunal directed the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded, this appeal is filed by the claimant.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant contended that the claimant had suffered fracture of NC: 2023:KHC-K:1450 medial condyle of right tibia and was conservatively treated at Government Hospital, Bidar.
He submitted that x-ray taken on 04.06.2013 demonstrated the same.

He further contended that the claimant was 35 years old and a driver by profession and the injuries had caused permanent functional disability and the Tribunal must have considered the evidence of PW.2 while assessing the functional disability.

He submitted that due to restriction of movement of right knee joint, the claimant was unable to do regular chores and hence, the Tribunal must have awarded adequate compensation under the conventional heads.
He also contended that the compensation awarded towards loss of amenities was extremely meager.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/insurer contended that the Tribunal had considered the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.8,000/-
per month while in similar circumstances this Court had considered the notional income at Rs.7,000/-
per month.
He therefore contends that the compensation NC: 2023:KHC-K:1450 awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not warrant any enhancement.
8. I have heard the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant as well as learned counsel for the respondent/insurer.
9. It is no doubt true that the notional income of a person injured or who died in a road traffic accident in the year 2013 is considered at a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month.
However, the insurer has not challenged the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal in considering the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.8,000/- per month.
Therefore, the insurer cannot challenge determination of the compensation by treating the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month.

10. It is seen that the claimant had suffered fracture of medial condyle of right tibia and having regard to the nature of his employment, it must have resulted in some disability and discomfort affecting his amenities.

Consequently, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal NC:
2023:KHC-K:1450 towards loss of amenities deserves to be enhanced by a sum of Rs.25,000/-.
11. Consequently, this appeal is allowed in part.
The compensation of Rs.2,22,100/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced by a sum of Rs.25,000/-.
